segments.title: 第149章 瑤池初上線,重燃現原形
segments.content:
Reigniting the Verdant Era, Chapter 149: The Premiere of Yao Chi, Chong Ran is Revealed

Early December.

In an office at Huayue Film & TV.

Zhai Senlei, the music producer, was reviewing the report sent by the finance department last month, as well as the various projected expenditures for this month.

When he flipped to the expenditure item related to song invitations, he scanned it casually, not planning to give it much thought.

But in the next second, his gaze froze, and his brow furrowed.

In recent years, Huayue Film & TV had gradually begun to cut many purely musical projects. Unless it was a singer-artist they were very optimistic about, even if they were to commission a song, it would at most be a single to test the waters.

More energy and resources had been completely shifted to film and television, especially dramas. In addition to traditional television series, they were also following the trends of the times in the online drama market.

For example, "Yao Chi Immortal Fate," which had just been released not long ago at the end of November, was being broadcast on iQiyi, with five episodes just uploaded.

The company's last major music-related project traced back to Yuan Wanqing's new album.

But it was clear that Yuan Wanqing's comeback had once again proven the correctness of the company's change in direction.

Consequently, the music department had gradually declined and was on the verge of becoming a subsidiary of the film and television department.

As the music producer, Zhai Senlei could do little about it. He had to do his job in his position, and what he could do now was to tighten expenditures in this area as much as possible, as instructed by the company.

But at this moment, on the report from the finance department, he saw the contract quotes for two songs.

One song, "Chaser of the Light," for 120,000.

One song, "Light," for 90,000.

Both were new songs signed by Yuan Wanqing.

This made Zhai Senlei's expression turn a little displeased.

After all, Yuan Wanqing's new album, a full ten songs, had cost several million yuan from start to finish.

If the promotion and distribution costs were included, it would be an even larger sum.

But the final result was clearly not great.

According to his estimates, they would probably have to wait until this time next year to recoup the costs of Yuan Wanqing's album, and only then could they make a small pittance.

If it hadn't been for Ying Zhicheng who had insisted against all opposition, deciding to try one more time, Huayue Film & TV might not even have renewed its contract with Yuan Wanqing.

How long had it been since then?

Why was she starting to commission new songs again?

Moreover, both songs came from the same producer.

Chong Ran… Zhai Senlei frowned, having no impression of this name at all.

Logically speaking, if they were to commission a song, given Yuan Wanqing's status, they should at least find some well-known producers in the industry.

To suddenly approach an unknown person, and not just for a buyout but with a revenue-sharing clause attached—although the percentage was very low—still made him even more dissatisfied.

If not for the detailed clause in Yuan Wanqing's contract with the company, which stipulated that Yuan Wanqing had a guaranteed budget for autonomously signing songs each month, Zhai Senlei would have probably put a stop to it long ago.

"Xiao Cao, come in."

Zhai Senlei called his assistant in and instructed, "Look up this songwriter named Chong Ran and report back to me in a bit."

"Okay."

A short while later, Assistant Xiao Cao returned, bringing a file and a copy of the contract for Zhai Senlei to review.

"This songwriter named Chong Ran has worked with our company once before," Xiao Cao said. "The theme song for 'Yao Chi Immortal Fate,' 'Annual Rings,' was written by him, but..."

"But what?"

"This songwriter seems to be only 15 years old..."

"What?" Zhai Senlei looked baffled. He opened the contract copy his assistant had brought him and then fell into deep thought. "Are you sure there's no mistake here?"

"That's what it says on the contract... For the specifics, we'd have to ask Ms. Yuan Wanqing. After all, she has the authority to sign songs independently, so we can't interfere with that."

"I understand." Zhai Senlei frowned and handed the file back. "You can go, there's nothing else."

"Producer Zhai, there's a music department meeting at ten o'clock this morning," Assistant Xiao Cao reminded him.

"Oh." Zhai Senlei's brow twitched. He reached out and tapped the desk. "Then leave that file on Chong Ran here with me for now."

As the calendar turned to December, the weather had clearly grown colder.

Although they still wore the same school uniform jackets and trousers outside, the students had swapped their short-sleeved shirts for sweaters and thermal pants underneath.

During English class, Li Luo, bored, quietly passed a draft notebook to Yan Zhusheng.

Li Luo: *Seems like "Yao Chi Immortal Fate" is out, you can watch it online. Have you seen it?*

Yan Zhusheng: *No, have you?*

Li Luo: *Watched a little.*

Yan Zhusheng: *Is it good?*

Li Luo: *Want the truth or a lie?*

Yan Zhusheng: *Both.*

Li Luo: *The lie is, the visuals are exquisite, and the production is excellent.*

Yan Zhusheng: *And the truth?*

Li Luo: *The plot is a pile of crap, truly hard to stomach. I absolutely cannot comprehend the scriptwriter's train of thought. Anyone with half a brain wouldn't be so brainless.*

Yan Zhusheng: *Does my mom's singing sound good?*

Li Luo: *Like a fresh flower stuck in a pile of cow dung.*

Teacher Ding Xiang, at the front of the classroom, was explaining the text and teaching new vocabulary for the unit when she caught a glimpse of the two students' antics by the window in the back row.

However, Li Luo was first in the class, and Yan Zhusheng's English ranked in the top three. Both of them had scored 140 on the English midterm exam.

So even though she saw Li Luo and Yan Zhusheng's little actions, Teacher Ding wasn't angry. She just smiled and called out, "Li Luo, which sentence were we just talking about?"

Suddenly being called upon, Li Luo wasn't flustered at all. As he stood up, the memory palace in his mind simultaneously replayed what Teacher Ding had just said about the text, and he fluently answered in English.

Teacher Ding coughed twice, motioned for him to sit down, and then continued with the lesson.

Well... she had deliberately called on Li Luo to answer the question.

It wasn't that she was targeting Li Luo. It was just that the first time she caught him slacking off, she hadn't known his English level, only to find the boy could answer fluently.

Later, she caught him zoning out in class several more times, called on him to answer questions, and he was still perfect.

This made Teacher Ding a little curious and a bit hooked. She thought, *There must be one time he isn't paying attention, right?*

But this time, she had clearly seen Li Luo excitedly passing notes and chatting with his deskmate, so how could he still answer?

Could someone really multitask in class like that?

Li Luo was unaware of Teacher Ding's thoughts. After answering the question, he behaved himself for a while.

The reason he was distracted in English class was mainly that he had already self-studied all the content for this semester. He had even borrowed Xu Youyu's textbook and flipped through all the subsequent English books.

For high school English, as long as one's vocabulary was large enough, it could solve 99% of the problems.

To him, English class had the lowest return on investment.

With that time in class, he might as well zone out and flip through the web novels he had read in his past life, then prepare the outline he needed for writing at night.

He chatted idly with Yan Zhusheng for a few sentences, and the class passed just like that.

Yan Zhusheng: *So have you seen the QQ Music comment section for "Annual Rings"?*

Near the end of class, Yan Zhusheng passed the draft notebook over, asking Li Luo a question.

Li Luo's brows furrowed, and a sense of unease grew in his heart.

Li Luo: *What's up with QQ Music? Is the reception bad?*

Yan Zhusheng: *No, it's about you.*

Li Luo: *Don't tell me someone is still flaming me? I just write the songs, I'm not the one singing.*

Yan Zhusheng: *Have you never even looked at the comment section over there?*

Asked this by Yan Zhusheng, Li Luo thought back and realized it seemed to be true.

He had only checked the song's play count and such when it was first released, and hadn't paid much attention to it afterward.

Let alone the comment section.

Li Luo: *So what's wrong with the comment section?*

Yan Zhusheng: *It was by reading the comment section that I found out you were writing the novel.*

Seeing this sentence, Li Luo felt as if he had been struck by lightning, and his entire body went stiff.

Li Luo: *Wait! It's not what my readers said, is it?*

Yan Zhusheng: *Mhm, they're all helping you promote it. They're all very nice people.*

Li Luo: "..."

An oversight in a flawless plan, a total oversight!

Li Luo had considered every possibility, but he really hadn't thought of this one.

But soon, Yan Zhusheng twisted the knife further.

Yan Zhusheng: *After "Yao Chi Immortal Fate" premiered, the version of "Annual Rings" sung by my mom was also released on QQ Music.*

Yan Zhusheng: *Now the comment section has both viewers of the drama and your readers.*

Yan Zhusheng: *That's why I wanted to ask, have the number of people reading your book increased recently?*

Looking at the draft notebook Yan Zhusheng passed over, the corner of Li Luo's mouth twitched.

Li Luo: *Is that the key issue here?*

Li Luo: *Your mom didn't see the comments, did she?*

Yan Zhusheng: *I don't know, I haven't asked.*

Li Luo: *Then don't ask! Absolutely do not ask!*

Yan Zhusheng: *Okay, I won't ask.*

Huayue Film & TV, inside a recording studio.

Luo Fei was leaning on the sofa, scrolling through her phone with great interest.

A short while later, Yuan Wanqing, looking exhausted after her meeting, pushed the door open and walked in. She flopped onto the sofa and let out a long sigh.

Just then, she noticed Luo Fei looking at her phone with the corners of her mouth turned up, smiling about something, so she asked, "What are you looking at? You look so happy."

"I discovered something interesting." Luo Fei patted her best friend's shoulder and prompted her, "Open your phone and check out the comment section for your song 'Annual Rings.' It's so interesting! Hahahaha!"

Seeing her laugh so loudly, Yuan Wanqing was puzzled, but she had a slight guess. "Are there a lot of people complaining about 'Yao Chi Immortal Fate'?"

"More than that. You'll know when you see it."

Yuan Wanqing raised an eyebrow, a little curious, and took out her phone to have a look.

When she clicked open the comment section, she was instantly stunned.

*Holy crap! Is this for real? Our Brother Ran is making it big, huh? A song he wrote actually got picked up by a TV drama?*

*My girlfriend was just complaining to me about this show today. I watched an episode with her, and when the theme song started, I was thinking, why does this sound so familiar!*

*I watched this with my wife. The lead actor, a 'little fresh meat,' is being aggressively marketed online, with several trending topics. The show is completely unwatchable. Only the song is decent.*

*This song comes from "I'm Really Not a Star," an original song by an author. In the novel, it also serves as the theme song for a TV drama.*

*LMAO! In the book, the protagonist gave this song away as a favor, and it ended up being paired with a huge flop of a xianxia drama! I hereby dub him the greatest prophet!*

*But to be fair, Yuan Wanqing's singing is pretty good, very evocative. It's a good song, but it's a shame the drama is so terrible.*

After reading the comments, Yuan Wanqing fell into a contemplative silence for a moment. "Luo Fei, which novel are they talking about?"

"This one." Luo Fei shook her phone, showing it to Yuan Wanqing. "Look, the author's name, Chong Ran. Isn't that the stage name Li Luo gave himself?"

"And look at the version of 'Annual Rings' sung by Zhusheng below. There are also quite a few comments from readers there, all saying it's a song written by the author himself."

"So that's Li Luo himself!"

Yuan Wanqing looked over all these clues, feeling a bit dazed.

"Li Luo also writes novels?"

"And it seems to be doing pretty well." Luo Fei tapped on the comment section. "Look at the comments, there are several hundred of them."

Yuan Wanqing leaned over for a look and nodded. Then her expression suddenly froze, and she pointed to the comment pinned at the very top by reader replies. "This 'Shengsheng Buxi'... couldn't be Zhusheng, could it? That's her screen name."

Luo Fei's eyebrows shot up, realizing it was true.

Shengsheng Buxi: *It's good. I prefer Mo Qinghan. Can you write more of her storyline?*

"Looks like Zhusheng knew all along," Luo Fei chuckled. "And she's a loyal reader, too."

Yuan Wanqing fell silent. After a long while, she downloaded the Qidian Reading app on her own phone.

"I'm going to see what he's written."

(End of this chapter)
